title: The decision stack
description: Five questions to verify you can compose all ten parts.

questions.prompt: On the flop, which check should you do FIRST in the decision cascade?
questions.explanation: SPR is the structural input that governs commitment. Compute it once at the start of the flop; everything else (texture, sizing, stack-off plan) depends on it.

questions.prompt: The turn brings a flush card on a board where you previously had range advantage. Which adjustment is most likely correct?

choices.text: Continue betting at the same frequency — flush cards don't matter.
Slow down on hands that don't have the flush; villain's range shifted toward more flushes and bluff-catchers.
Always overbet to bluff villain off the flush.

questions.explanation: Scare cards rebalance both ranges. Slow down with hands that don't make the new draw, and choose your bluff candidates from hands that block villain's strongest continues.

questions.prompt: On the river against a calling station, you should still aim for the GTO bluff:value ratio so as not to be exploitable.
questions.explanation: The GTO ratio is unexploitable. Against a station who under-folds, bluffs lose money — drop the bluff frequency below GTO, often to zero.

questions.prompt: When facing a 3/4-pot bet on the river with a bluff-catcher, which inputs should you weigh? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Pot odds — what equity do I need to call?
Player type — does villain bluff at GTO frequency?
Blockers — does my hand block villain's value range?

questions.explanation: Pot odds, opponent tendency, and blockers are the three inputs. Chip suit is irrelevant. Note that MDF is *not* on the list — it's a theoretical floor, not a calling threshold.

questions.prompt: When two parts of the curriculum disagree (e.g. MDF says call, by-worse criterion says fold), which framework wins?

choices.text: Always MDF — it's the GTO baseline.
Whichever framework matches an explicit EV calculation against villain's range.

questions.explanation: EV is the parent quantity. MDF, pot odds, by-worse and α are all derivations under different assumptions. When they conflict, recompute EV against the actual villain range and follow the answer.
